title: Normality descends from saturated completed strict-local monoid models
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] over $x$, and put $A_0=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$, the affine pointed-etale-neighbourhood colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let $\widehat A=\varprojlim_m A/\mathfrak m_A^m$ be the completion at its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively and sharp (its only invertible element is $0$), and $n\geq0$. For a local coefficient ring $L$, define $B_L(P,n)$ as the completion of $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$; the monoid ring consists of finite sums with $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. Suppose $\widehat A$ is isomorphic as a ring either to $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$, or to $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$, where $C$ is a Cohen ring of residue characteristic the prime $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. Then the canonical maps $A_0\to A$ and $A\to\widehat A$ are faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and $\widehat A$, $A$ and $A_0$ are normal domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. No log structure or log regularity is assumed on $X$ beyond the displayed completed-ring hypothesis.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$ containing $x$, with corresponding prime $\mathfrak p$. By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the germ map identifies $A_0=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] at the multiplicative set $R\setminus\mathfrak p$. Thus $A_0$ is a Noetherian local ring.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); affine stalk identification: schemes.tex, Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves).

proof.text: Let $K\subset\Omega$ be the separable algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$ in $\Omega$. It is a separable closure of $\kappa(x)$ by [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure], since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed; and $\kappa(x)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field of the local ring $A_0=R_{\mathfrak p}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] to the ring $A_0$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak pA_0$ and $K$: the category of pointed etale triples of $A_0$ is filtered, and its colimit $H$, with structural map $\rho:A_0\to H$, is a local ring. By [lem-sc-etale-triples-colimit-is-strict-henselization] (at the closed point, with $\chi:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to K$ the inclusion), $H$ with this colimit cocone is an algebraic strict henselization of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ relative to $K$. Apply [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] to the affine open immersion $i:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ with image $U$, the geometric point $\bar x$, $L=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $L^{\mathrm{sh}}=H$. It gives a ring isomorphism $\theta:A\to H$ with $\theta\circ a=\rho\circ\lambda$, where $a:R\to A$ is the chart leg and $\lambda:R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization map, and it states that $A$ is a strictly henselian local ring. The canonical map $A_0\to A$, composed with the germ map $\lambda$, is the chart leg $a$: both are the map on sections over $U$ of the structural morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, which factors through $U$. Hence $\theta\circ(A_0\to A)$ and $\rho$ agree after precomposition with $\lambda$, so they are equal by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property].

source.place: Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different), identification of the triple colimit at a prime with the strict henselization of the localization; etale-cohomology.tex, Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), affine-neighbourhood proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] to the local ring $A_0$, $K$ and the colimit cocone of Step 2: the structural map $\rho:A_0\to H$ is faithfully flat. By Step 2 the canonical map $A_0\to A$ equals $\theta^{-1}\circ\rho$, and $\theta^{-1}$ is a ring isomorphism, so $A$ and $H$ are isomorphic $A_0$-modules and $A_0\to A$ is faithfully flat. Since $A_0$ is Noetherian (Step 1), [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian], applied to the strict henselization $H$ of $A_0$, gives that $H$ is Noetherian, hence so is $A\cong H$. $A$ is local by Step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] to $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$: its completion is exactly the inverse limit $\widehat A$ in the statement, so $A\to\widehat A$ is faithfully flat as well.

The hypotheses on $P$, $n$, and the coefficient ring are precisely those of [lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality]. In the field case apply its case (i); in the Cohen case apply its case (ii), using the given congruence $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. It gives that the displayed model is a nonzero normal domain. Transport this property along the assumed ring isomorphism to obtain that $\widehat A$ is a normal domain. This application requires no log structure on $X$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, displayed complete models; agent assembly using the independently stated saturated-model normality theorem.

proof.text: We descend normal-domain normality along each of the two maps of Step 3, first $A\to\widehat A$, then $A_0\to A$. For either map $f:R\to S$ with $S$ already a normal domain, [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] gives injectivity, so $R$ is a nonzero domain: $1_R=0$ or $ab=0$ would imply respectively $1_S=0$ or $f(a)f(b)=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fraction-field-lift], the composite $R\hookrightarrow S\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(S)$ extends to an injection of fraction fields, sending $a/b$ to $f(a)/f(b)$. If $a/b$ is integral over $R$, its monic equation maps to a monic equation over $S$, so this fraction lies in $S$ by normality [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Hence $f(a)\in f(b)S$, and ideal contraction for $I=bR$ gives $a\in bR$. Writing $a=br$ shows $a/b=r\in R$. Thus $R$ is integrally closed in its fraction field. The two applications prove that $A$ and $A_0$ are normal domains, completing all conclusions.
